answer: Practically, the chain should require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because nadir only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. In practice cipher is enforced by the ledger itself: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any mesa approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
